newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks lose ahead of U.S. Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks lose ahead of U.S. Fed meeting.

text.p: Hong Kong's key share index lost almost one percent on Tuesday as sellers moved in ahead of the U.S. central bank policy meeting on interest rates, brokers said.
Tokyo stocks barely moved, off just 0.04 percent, but Seoul's bourse led the losers in Asia, ending 1.57 percent down at its fifth consecutive three-year closing low.
Brokers in Hong Kong said the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting later on Tuesday prompted the selloff.
"The FOMC is just an excuse to take profit," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities. "U.S. inflation is under control and we won't see a rise in rates."
The Hang Seng Index closed down 122.11 points, or 0.94 percent, at 12,815.37.
Brokers said as the market's turnover declined, prices were more vulnerable to single large orders and large players.
"There are not a lot of natural buyers around at this time of year," said one broker with a large U.S. house. "And there aren't any shorts either."
Tokyo stocks ended mixed in narrow range trade, the key 225-issue Nikkei average finishing 8.58 points, or 0.04 percent, lower at 20,413.46.
Brokers said early losses were mostly offset by fresh buying and short-covering in sectors that had been hammered recently, such as construction and banking.
"Foreign securities houses placed a fairy large amount of buying in banks...which triggered more buying," said a trader at a foreign securities house.
The Seoul bourse fell sharply as nervous investors sold believing there no relief in sight to the market's downward trend, brokers said.
The composite stock index fell 10.57 points to a provisional close of 663.35. This was the lowest close since March 29, 1993, when the index ended at 652.21.

"Most people are very upset about the market and are getting a little panicked," said Casey Choe, a UBS Securities broker. "Many brokers feel the market will fall to 650 and some say as low as 620 before the floor is found."

Brokers said fundamental problems such as the uncertain economic outlook, high interest rates, and a floundering won made the stock market an unattractive proposition for many investors, especially foreigners.
Thai stocks closed slightly lower as investors sold some large capitalised stocks after they termed as unclear the finance minister's statement on how to boost the economy, brokers said.
The SET index slipped 5.53 points, or 0.63 percent, to 867.23.
Late selling pulled Taiwan share prices to close lower, the weighted index ending 35.85 points, or 0.52 percent, lower at 6,855.57.
Philippine shares closed down for the second straight session as investors were kept at bay by a weak Dow Jones index and fears over the FOMC meeting, traders said.
The main index finished 22.37 points, or 0.72 percent, lower at 3,093.21 points.
In Bombay, the key share index rose 26.56 points, or 0.90 percent, to 2,985.21.
At 1115 GMT the dollar was trading at 1.5461/66 marks and 113.73/3.83 yen.
Hong Kong bullion ended at US$367.60/368.10 an ounce against New York's US$367.80/368.30 close on Monday.
Asian oil prices were slightly lower, with SIMEX February Brent crude futures last trading at $23.67 a barrel, down 13 cents from London's Monday close.
